canonical_fact: Accumulation is the on-chain phase that invokes service Accumulate logic for available work results and applies permitted changes to service and selected protocol state.
misconceptions: Accumulation is only a data-availability vote.
title: Accumulation

canonical_fact: JAM state keeps available but not-yet-accumulated work reports in a ready queue when dependencies prevent immediate execution.
misconceptions: Every available work report must be accumulated immediately even if prerequisites are missing.

relations.statement: Reports remain in the ready queue while valid prerequisites are still unfulfilled.

title: Ready queue

canonical_fact: JAM retains roughly an epoch of recently accumulated work-package hashes so dependency satisfaction can be determined.

relations.statement: Recent accumulated-package hashes are used to remove satisfied dependencies before selecting accumulatable reports.

title: Accumulated history

canonical_fact: A work report with a prerequisite that has not yet accumulated is deferred rather than accumulated immediately.
title: Unfulfilled dependency

canonical_fact: A work report whose dependency is known invalid is cancelled rather than waiting indefinitely for that dependency.
title: Invalid dependency

canonical_fact: JAM derives an order of accumulatable reports by repeatedly selecting reports whose dependency sets are empty and updating remaining dependency sets.
title: Accumulation priority

canonical_fact: Accumulation has a limited per-block gas budget, so not every ready work result is necessarily processed in one block.
title: Accumulation gas budget

canonical_fact: Work items for the same service are aggregated into a shared PVM Accumulate invocation to amortize setup cost.
misconceptions: JAM always launches one fresh Accumulate PVM instance per work item and never batches by service.
title: Service batching

canonical_fact: JAM combines sequential report processing for gas accounting with service-grouped parallel accumulation rounds for efficiency.
title: Sequential and parallel accumulation

canonical_fact: Accumulation converts each work digest plus report context into an operand tuple carrying package, segment-root, authorizer, payload-hash, gas, trace and result information.
title: Operand tuple

canonical_fact: A deferred transfer is an accumulation input representing a service-to-service token transfer with amount, destination mode, memo and gas allowance.
misconceptions: A deferred transfer is applied immediately inside Refine.

relations.statement: The transfer host call produces deferred transfers that later participate in accumulation.

title: Deferred transfer

canonical_fact: A deferred transfer includes a fixed-size memo payload that is delivered as part of the receiver-side accumulation context.
title: Transfer memo

canonical_fact: Accumulation operates over the mutable state subset containing service accounts, staging validator keys, authorizer queues and privilege-related service identities.
title: Accumulation partial state

canonical_fact: If a service and its supervisor mutate the same service state in one optimistic parallel round, JAM discards the conflicting service execution results according to the accumulation rules.
title: Supervisor mutation conflict

canonical_fact: Deferred transfers are scheduled to avoid unsafe parallel execution with supervisor logic because transfer effects cannot simply be discarded without losing funds.
title: Transfer conflict handling

canonical_fact: Privileged always-accumulating services receive a configured gas allowance to execute accumulation each block even without ordinary work digests.
title: Always-accumulating service

canonical_fact: Refine computes work results without directly committing global state changes; state mutation is concentrated in on-chain accumulation and its host-call semantics.

relations.statement: This separation is a central part of JAM's in-core/on-chain dualism.
Refine is on the non-state-writing side of the JAM execution boundary.
Accumulate is the stateful side of the JAM execution boundary.

title: State-write boundary

canonical_fact: A work item's Refine result is first recorded in a work digest and work report, must pass guaranteeing and availability, and only then can its service-level implications be processed by Accumulate.
title: Result-to-state flow
